issue_context.title: DataFrame.replace changes dtype of columns not containing any value to be replaced.
issue_context.body:
#### Code Sample, a copy-pastable example if possible

```python
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
data = pd.DataFrame({'A':np.nan,'B':1.096, 'C':1}, index=[0])
data.replace(to_replace={np.nan:None}, inplace=True)

```
#### Problem description

Checking data.dtypes before and after the call to replace shows that the datatype of column B changed from float to object whereas that of C stayed at int. If I remove column A from the original data that does not happen.

When using replace I expected columns without any matching value not to be touched / changed. 



#### Expected Output

Dtype of column 'B' should remain 'float64'.

comments: Thanks for the report, can confirm this reproduces on `master` - interested in investigating the issue / submitting a PR?

I think the problem here is that both `np.nan` and `1.096` are part of the same `FloatBlock` and so in
```
self = self.coerce_to_target_dtype(value)
```
from `pandas.core.internals.blocks.py`, the entire block is getting coerced to the target dtype (object)
